meta.title: Technology Selection Matrix
meta.sub: You leave this session with: Chapter 5 — what you chose, what you rejected, and why — completing PT1

moves.detail: Read Ch. 5 of the Carmen Market study. Count the rejections.
Every option — including the four from Weeks 4–7.
ADOPT / REJECT / N-A, with a reason on every single row.
Every N/A needs a ‘because’. Fix the lazy ones.
Partner hunts for a technology you forced in.
PT1 is now complete. File the whole dossier.

model.label: THE MODEL — how the Carmen Market study did it
model.html:
Their matrix has six rows and only ONE adoption. Four rejections and one retained fallback.

The row that matters most: “IoT / robotics / AR-VR — N/A, justified rejection. None of these apply to a payments-adoption problem. Listed here only to show the discipline was applied, not skipped.”

They also kept cash as a permanent fallback — not a transition phase. Rejecting your own course's flashiest technologies, in writing, is the mark of a serious study.

steps.label: STEP 1 — Your matrix
steps.instruction: Fill every row. The Weeks 4–7 rows are compulsory — you must state whether each applies, and ‘N/A, because…’ is worth full marks.

steps.label: STEP 2 — The status quo row
steps.instruction: What happens to the current way of doing things? The Carmen Market study kept cash permanently, on purpose.

options.note: Make sure this is really warranted — if there's any user segment that can't or won't switch, a full replacement is a risk you haven't priced yet.
A transition-period safety net. Say plainly when the fallback is expected to end, or why it won't.
The Carmen Market study's own choice — cash, forever, for whoever needs it. Not a failure of ambition; a recognition that some adopters never come along.

steps.label: STEP 2 (cont.) — The reason
steps.instruction: State the current method and justify your choice.
steps.prefix: The current method (paper, cash, word of mouth…) will be replaced / kept as fallback / kept permanently — because:

steps.label: STEP 3 — PT1 assembly check
steps.instruction: Tick only what is genuinely filed. An unticked box now is a warning; an untrue tick is a problem.

trap.label: THE TRAP
trap.html: The trap is the opposite of what you expect: it is not rejecting too much, it is forcing technologies IN. Teams add IoT sensors to a paperwork problem because they think using more of the course content earns more marks. It earns fewer. The AI-blockchain-drone project is a real and recognisable failure, and this matrix exists specifically to stop it. A justified rejection is worth exactly as much as an adoption.

peer_check.label: PEER CHECK
peer_check.instruction: Swap with another team. Their job is not to be nice — it is to find the specific weakness named below.
peer_check.task: Look for a technology they ADOPTED that their Chapter 1 problem does not actually need. Name it here, and ask them which sentence of Chapter 1 requires it. If they cannot point to one, it is decoration.

file_it.label: FILE IT
file_it.instruction: Date it, initial it, and add it to your team's dossier folder. A chapter that is not filed does not exist.
